Additionally, feedback stabilization of the laser launch will contribute to improving late-time data quali- ty. These two improvements will require a complete overhaul of the current design to accommodate the increased laser power and fast dynamic feedback of the lasers. Through the LDRD program, basic research will be conducted to determine the most probable causes of late-time data loss. The lessons learned will help drive future diagnostic improvements. Beyond improvements to the existing optical diagnostics, 32 DCX STRATEGY new universal fiber Bragg gratings will be developed for use on all experiments requiring HE burn measurements. The gratings will allow measurements for both short- and long-distance measurements without loss of resolution and with simple post-shot analysis. Another potential area of interest is in situ measurements of detonator performance in an experiment. This would elimi- nate uncertainty in timing by giving a direct measurement of detonator performance as opposed to a statistical analysis of a representative set of detonators. The diagnostics being considered are very preliminary but are high risk/high reward and would represent a breakthrough in experimental timing. Hydro Data Management The combination of digital radiography and laser/fiber-optic diagnostics systems has expanded hydro data from kilobytes to terabytes. This massive increase in data volume requires the development of updated methods to ensure enduring data availability for future generations of weapon designers. To accomplish this: • Hydro data archives of record will be stored in an electronic document management system (EDMS) per DOE requirements • Essential metadata will be collected and attached to the data in the EDMS • A uniform file directory structure will be used across all hydrotests, and previous hydrotests will be migrated as resources permit • Raw data will be uniformly protected as read and/or copy only • Data integrity checks will be consistently performed as copies are made to prevent data file corruption, from inception to final repository In addition, supporting information essential to
